# Evidence card — Remember to do it later

Cue-action pairing draws on general-population if-then planning research. Prospective memory difficulties in ADHD are reported at group level. AI reminders have not been tested.

Use only these claims, within the scope stated. None of them tested this software.

- **CLM-RS-IMPL-INTENTIONS** (checked against an abstract or summary only): In general-population research, forming if-then plans (implementation intentions) had a medium-to-large average effect on goal attainment across 94 tests (Gollwitzer & Sheeran, 2006, d = .65). This is adjacent evidence for cue-action pairing. It is not ADHD-specific and not evidence for this software.
  Source: [Implementation Intentions and Goal Achievement: A Meta-analysis of Effects and Processes](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0065-2601(06)38002-1).
- **CLM-RS-PM-ADHD** (checked against an abstract or summary only): In a 2026 experiment with 196 adults (98 with ADHD), Stelz, Edel and Altgassen found lower everyday prospective memory in the ADHD group, and found that episodic future thinking (vividly imagining carrying out an intention) at encoding improved performance compared with standard encoding. This is lab-assigned encoding instruction over three sessions, not evidence for this software.
  Source: [The impact of process- versus outcome-focused episodic future thinking on everyday prospective memory in individuals with and without attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)](https://doi.org/10.1037/xap0000586); [Episodic Future Thinking Improves Everyday Prospective Memory Performance in Adults With a Previous Diagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder by Community Providers](https://doi.org/10.1177/10870547261416467).

Full register, statuses and limitations: `evidence/claims.yaml` in the source repository. Runtime snapshot: `references/shared/runtime-evidence.md`. No claim has been reviewed by a clinician.
